bottom_line: In PLATO, ticagrelor versus clopidogrel reduced the 12-month primary composite of death from vascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke (hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.77 to 0.92).
implications: These data support that ticagrelor, compared with clopidogrel, was associated with a lower 12-month Kaplan–Meier rate of the composite of death from vascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke (9.8% vs. 11.7%; hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.77 to 0.92) while showing no significant difference in major bleeding by study criteria (11.6% vs. 11.2%; P=0.43), but a higher rate of non–CABG-related major bleeding (4.5% vs. 3.8%; P=0.03). The result does not support a difference in stroke alone (1.5% vs. 1.3%, P = 0.22).

major_points.text: Multicenter, double-blind randomized trial in patients hospitalized with acute coronary syndrome (with or without ST-segment elevation).
major_points.quote: In this multicenter, double-blind, randomized trial, we compared ticagrelor... and clopidogrel... in 18,624 patients admitted to the hospital with an acute coronary syndrome, with or without ST-segment elevation.

major_points.text: Ticagrelor dosing was 180 mg loading then 90 mg twice daily; clopidogrel was 300–600 mg loading then 75 mg daily.
major_points.quote: ticagrelor (180-mg loading dose, 90 mg twice daily thereafter) and clopidogrel (300-to-600-mg loading dose, 75 mg daily thereafter)

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was time to first composite of death from vascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy variable was the time to the first occurrence of composite of death from vascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint occurred in 9.8% vs 11.7% at 12 months (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.77–0.92; P<0.001).

subgroups.text: Effects explored in 25 prespecified subgroups and 8 post hoc subgroups, without adjustment for multiple comparisons.
subgroups.quote: The consistency of effects on effi- cacy and safety end points was explored in 25 prespecified subgroups and 8 post hoc sub- groups, without adjustment for multiple com- parisons.

subgroups.text: Primary endpoint subgroup analyses did not show significant heterogeneity with three exceptions.
subgroups.quote: The results regarding the primary end point did not show significant heterogeneity in analy- ses of the 33 subgroups, with three exceptions

harms.text: Fatal intracranial bleeding was higher with ticagrelor.
Dyspnea was more common with ticagrelor (13.8% vs 7.8%).
Premature discontinuation because of adverse event occurred more often with ticagrelor (7.4% vs 6.0%).
Major bleeding did not differ significantly (11.6% vs 11.2%; P=0.43).
Ventricular pauses ≥3 sec in first week were higher with ticagrelor (5.8% vs 3.6%).
Nonintracranial fatal bleeding was lower with ticagrelor (0.1% vs 0.3%; P=0.03).
